claims.claim_text: Training and testing of ligand-binding-site predictors is often performed on one holo structure as a representative. The paper presents this as unrealistic because the apo form may differ from the holo binding-site geometry.
The database provides pocket-level apo/holo annotations that can be used to train or evaluate ligand-binding-site predictors. This is one of the motivating use cases behind the resource.
The database can be used to train and evaluate machine-learning tools. The paper specifically connects this to ligand-binding-site prediction and structural comparison.
Protein conformational variability is captured by AHoJ-DB through its systematic pairing of apo and holo crystal structures for the same protein, making the variability explicitly queryable.

term_str: λDrug design and docking.(Drug design and docking · Protein structure)

claims.claim_text: The paper argues that docking and drug-design studies often still use mostly rigid holo structures. This can miss conformational diversity relevant to binding and prediction.

term_str: λProtein conformational variability.(Ligand · (Protein conformational variability · Binding pocket))

claims.claim_text: A ligand defines the binding pocket in the holo structure: the set of protein residues within a distance cutoff of the bound ligand constitutes the pocket, making the ligand the operational reference for pocket identification.

Protein conformational variability shapes the binding pocket: differences in side-chain and backbone geometry between apo and holo states directly alter pocket volume, shape, and electrostatic environment.
